content.comment_body: In [product_name] version [version_no], when you press F2 to view memory allocations, you see a line stating "Maximum nesting depth: M16-Q3". What is the meaning of this?

Hello, Some earlier releases of [product_name] only supported a maximum nesting depth of 7 function blocks. If you needed more, you had to use a flag or a Q variable. Nesting depth refers to the number of function blocks contained within a single line. Hope this clarification helps.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is seeking clarification about the 'Maximum nesting depth: M16-Q3' message seen in the memory allocation screen of [product_name], expressing uncertainty regarding the terminology used. Another participant with more experience explains historical limitations in older versions and explains nesting depth as the number of function blocks stacked in a single instruction line.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect software to provide clear and understandable explanations for technical terms and limitations, especially regarding concepts like nesting depth.
